title: Edgible card
description: Source of truth for a shareable pattern. A valid card has no device name, device id, hostname, organization id, password, or volume data.

name.description: Name of the card, the same as its directory.

type.description: app: one self-hosted app, the building block, always tested. pattern: several apps wired together for a purpose, built from app cards.

added.description: The date the card was added to the catalog, YYYY-MM-DD. Shown on the site, and used for its recently added list.

homepage.description: The app's own home page, such as its website or documentation. Shown on the card's page.

license.description: The app's licence as an SPDX identifier, such as AGPL-3.0-only or MIT. Shown on the card's page. Leave it out when unsure.

status.description: experimental: newly made, less proven. stable: the default when this is left out. deprecated: still here but do not start new setups on it; the README says what replaces it, and reason says why. The tools do not offer it, and deploy_card refuses it.

steward.description: The GitHub user or organisation that answers for this card: reviews changes to it, approves its upgrades, fixes it when its test fails, and can be reached through its issues. Shown on the card's page, linked to github.com/<steward>. Leave it out when nobody does, and the card is shown as having no steward.

reviewed.description: The date a person last read the card and its test, YYYY-MM-DD. Shown with the steward. Leave it out when unknown.

replaced-by.description: For a deprecated card: the card that replaces it. Shown on the card's page.

reason.description: For a deprecated card: why, in a sentence for the person, such as what Edgible cannot do for it yet. Shown on the card's page and by the tools, which do not offer the card for new setups.

contact.description: Optional. A public way to reach whoever looks after the card, of their own choosing: an https address (a page, a chat or a form) or an email address, such as a role address. It is public and permanent in git history, so use one you are happy to have scraped, not a personal or account sign-in address. Shown on the card's page next to the steward.

data.description: Optional. What the card's volumes hold, how to copy them consistently, and how to tell the data is there. It comes before places:, which test-card --write-places rewrites. card.env is always data and needs no entry.

volumes.description: One entry per named volume in the card's Compose files.

fingerprint.description: Required when a volume is irreplaceable. Run in service, read-only and quick, it prints one line of JSON: counts (integers) and dates (ISO), never content, such as {"bookmarks": 412, "latest": "2026-10-14"}. An empty install prints zeros.

secrets.description: Optional. Every secret the card uses, by the variable that holds it: what kind it is, how it is made, and what happens to it on a move. Internal and human secrets are made on the device by the card-secrets service at first start, never written in card.env or the Compose file; shared and external ones come from card.env or the person's chosen provider.

places.description: Optional. For each place: the minimum recommended machine, and for a place no app uses, the Compose files it runs. Keys are place names.

name.description: Application name. Copied from metadata.name of edgible application export.

what.description: What this program is. Two apps that are one process say so here.

from.description: Image name, or for an app in a native place, the release it installs, such as https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.40.4. An existing-app export does not record it. Read it from docker ps by matching the port. No device and no organization.

database.description: Database image in the same Compose file, when the program does not run alone.

port.description: Host port. Copied from the workload containerPort of the export.

verifyPath.description: The path test-card asks for when it checks the published hostname, default /. For an app with no page at /, such as a backend that only serves an API.

protocol.description: https for web apps. tcp or udp for apps that are not web, such as a game server or SSH; those have no auth mode, so authModes is [none], and their port is from 20000 to 29999.

subtype.description: The process is already listening on this port before the stack file is deployed.

authModes.description: none is the auth mode None. An export that says edgible-login is written org.

place.description: Topology name, not a device name and not a device id. Applications with the same place run on one serving device. Two applications that are one process share a place, a port, and a from.

publicFor.description: What needs the app on auth mode none, in everyday words, such as "its browser extension" or "its phone apps": clients that are not a web browser cannot pass Edgible's sign-in, so they stop working while the app is kept on org. Absent when nothing is known to need it.

paths.description: URL paths, each exact (/identity/connect/token) or ending in * for everything below it (/api/*).

for.description: What calls these paths and what protects them, in everyday words, such as "the Bitwarden apps' vault calls, each with a Vaultwarden token". Edgible records it as the reason for the exception.

appPaths.description: Paths left to the app's own login while the rest of the app stays behind Edgible's sign-in (org): for clients that are not a web browser, such as phone apps and browser extensions, which cannot pass Edgible's sign-in. Edgible declares each as a path policy with auth mode app-native. Only with org in authModes; in place of publicFor, which publishes the whole app. An app with setup: gets them once its setup is done, so its open sign-up is never reachable through them.

behind.description: The auth mode the app is published on while a person finishes its own setup, such as an install wizard. Only the organization reaches it. When setup is done, it is switched to authModes, or stays when authModes is [org].

done.description: A shell command, run on the device with card.env exported and $COMPOSE set, that exits 0 once the app's own setup is finished, such as $COMPOSE --profile cli run --rm -T wordpress-cli wp core is-installed.

during.description: card.env values the app starts with until done exits 0, such as {NEXTAUTH_DISABLE_SIGNUP: "false"} so the person can make the first account, which becomes the admin. Then the app restarts with card.env as written (sign-up off) before it is switched to authModes. Each key is set in card.env.

setup.description: The app sets itself up on its first visit. It is published behind org, a person runs its own setup on its real hostname, and it is switched to authModes once done exits 0. The card's test does the setup with test/setup.sh.

url.description: The address the app gives out, as its Compose file builds it, with ${VAR}, ${VAR:-default} and ${VAR:?message} filled in from card.env, such as https://wordpress.${ORG_LABEL}.${EDGIBLE_DOMAIN:-edgible.app}.

setting.description: The card.env line that overrides url, such as WORDPRESS_URL: set it to give the app another address (your own domain).

change.description: A shell command for an app that also keeps its address in its data, run on the device after the restart with card.env exported, $COMPOSE set, and $OLD_URL and $NEW_URL, such as $COMPOSE --profile cli run --rm -T wordpress-cli wp search-replace "$OLD_URL" "$NEW_URL" --all-tables --skip-columns=guid.

address.description: The app keeps its own address, so a new one (your own domain, a move) needs more than a new hostname at the edge. set-address changes it this way and checks the app answers at the new address without sending people to the old one. Leave it out when the app does not keep its address.

source.description: Optional. Where the source of the app's image is, for an app a person may want to change and rebuild. The README gets a Customising section from it. Leave it out for an app whose source is not meant to be changed.

repo.description: The repository that holds the code and the Dockerfile the image is built from, such as https://github.com/example/app. It is the repository the image names in its org.opencontainers.image.source label.

ref.description: The tag or commit the pinned image was built from, so a person starts from the code that runs. Leave it out when the repository's default branch is the code.

path.description: The directory of the repository that is the build context. Default: the root.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile, relative to the build context. Default: Dockerfile.

dev.description: The command that runs the app from source with its demo data, for trying a change before building an image, such as bun run dev.

memory.description: Memory for everything in the place together.

disk.description: Disk for the images and the data to start with.

arch.description: CPU architectures every image in the place runs on.

gpu.description: Whether the place needs a GPU.

runs.description: The Compose files this place runs. Required for a place no app uses: one that runs only services that connect out, such as a CI runner or a backup job. Such a place starts after Publish.

native.description: The place runs its app natively on this OS, not in Docker: install.sh installs a pinned release and starts it as a service, uninstall.sh removes everything it installed. For an app that needs the machine itself, such as Ollama on a Mac's GPU, which Docker on macOS cannot reach. A native place has no runs:.

class.description: irreplaceable: back it up and check it after a restore. rebuildable: the app recreates it from irreplaceable data, such as a search index. cache: safe to drop, such as thumbnails.

dump.description: A consistent copy without stopping the app. Without it, a consistent copy stops the app.

command.description: Run in service, it writes the dump to stdout.

restore.description: Run in service, it reads the dump from stdin.

command.description: Run with sh -c in service, with that container's environment.

service.description: A service in one of the card's Compose files.

kind.description: internal: only the app's own services need it; shared: apps of the card on different machines; human: a person needs it once, to sign in or call an API; external: someone else issued it and the person brings it.

use.description: For internal secrets: what it protects, which sets what happens on a move.

make.description: The shell command that prints a new value, such as openssl rand -hex 16. Not for external secrets.

on-move.description: Optional. What a move or restore does with it. Defaults by kind and use: new for signing and token, new-then-update for password, carry for everything else.

update.description: For new-then-update: the command that applies a new value to the data, run in service, such as an ALTER USER for a database password.

for.description: For human secrets: what the person uses it for, shown with it once.

from.description: For external secrets: where the person gets one, such as a URL.

required.description: For external secrets: false when the card runs without it. Default true.
